To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the order of Hininf controllers for descriptor systems is independent of (i.e., invariant under) a descriptor realization and (ii) the order of such controllers can be reduced by taking into account the unstable finite zeros and infinite zeros

the order of a proper Hinfin controller for a descriptor generalized plant can be reduced to a lower bound, which is independent on a descriptor realization of this generalized plant, and that the lower bound is equal to the sum of the number of unstable finite zeros and the number of infinite zeros of the generalized plant.

the order of Hininfilters for a descriptor system can be reduced to a bound that is independent of (or invariant under the allowed transformations) a descriptor realization, and that the bound is equal to the number of unstable finite zeros or the number of infinite zeros.
In summary, our research is concerned with
reduced-order proper Hininfilters/controllers for descriptor systems, which are a natural generalization of state-space systems.
the design of reduced-order Hinfin controller for descriptor systems.
the following issues: 1) The existence and design of Hinfin controllers with reduced-order for descriptor systems; 2) The order reduction mechanism of Hinfin controllers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hinfin control theory for descriptor systems has been established on a solid theoretical foundation, and that it has been extended to a wide range of applications in the field of engineering.
the Hinfin controller design problem for descriptor systems is not more complex than the Hinfin control design problem for state-space systems.

, in the case that the generalized plant has unstable finite zeros or/and infinite zeros, the order of Hininf controllers can be reduced through the use of an appropriate descriptor realization of the plant, and this reduction is not limited by the order of the descriptor realization of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reduced-order Hinfin control problem can be solved for descriptor systems by using a similar approach to that for state-space systems, but the order of the Hinfin controller for a descriptor system is bounded by the number of its unstable finite zeros and/or infinite zeros.

, for the descriptor systems under consideration, we can always design reduced-order Hinfin proper controllers of the order no larger than that of the generalized plant, which is a significant improvement over the existing results.

, in the case of Hinfin controller synthesis, we have shown that the order of the controller is determined by the order of the generalized plant and the number of unstable finite zeros of the generalized plant (if any).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the order of Hininf controllers for descriptor systems is independent of the descriptor realization of the system.

the order of Hininf controllers can be reduced to a level that is independent of a descriptor realization of a generalized plant by considering the unstable finite zeros and the infinite zeros of the descriptor plant.
, in the Hinfin control of descriptor systems, the order of Hininfilters and controllers is independent of the number of finite zeros or infinite poles of a descriptor system.
